rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious usage, taqwa is protecting the soul from what harms it in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والتقوى في عرف الشرع وقاية النفس عما يضرها في الآخرة وهي على مراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first level avoids everlasting punishment by disavowing idolatry.
rows.anchor: الأولى التوقي عن العذاب المخلد بالتبري من الشرك وعليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second, commonly called taqwa, means avoiding every sin.
rows.anchor: والثانية التجنب عن كل إثم وهو المتعارف باسم التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest, true taqwa is withdrawing from everything that distracts one from God.
rows.anchor: والثالثة التنزه عن جميع ما يشغله وهو التقوى الحقيقي المطلوب بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ذو النون المصري
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun told a ministerial retainer seeking spiritual aspiration that fearing God as he feared the ruler would make him one of the truthful saints.
rows.anchor: عن ذي النون المصري أنه لما جاء إليه بغض الوزراء وطلب الهمة وأظهر الخشية من السلطان قال له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritual wayfarer should fear the Lord and remain watchful of God in every state.
rows.anchor: فينبغي للسالك أن يتقي ربه ويراقب الله في جميع أحواله كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muraqaba is the servant's knowledge that the Lord sees him; keeping that awareness present is watchfulness, the root of all good.
rows.anchor: والمراقبة : علم العبد باطلاع الرب سبحانه عليه فاستدامته لهذا العلم مراقبة لربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reaches watchfulness only after self-accounting, correcting the present, following truth, guarding the heart and each breath with God, and watching all one's states.
rows.anchor: إلا بعد فراغه من المحاسبة فإذا حاسب نفسه على ما سلف وأصلح حاله في الوقت ولازم طريق الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting God's constant awareness leaves one far from even the beginning of spiritual connection, let alone true nearness.
rows.anchor: ومن تغافل عن هذه الجملة فهو بمعزل عن بداية الوصلة فكيف عن حقائق القربة

rows.speaker: حميد الطويل
rows.claim: Humayd warned that sinning in private while believing God sees is grave audacity, while thinking God does not see is disbelief.
rows.anchor: قال سليمان بن علي لحميد الطويل : عظني

rows.speaker: بعض الصالحين
rows.claim: A righteous teacher explained his special attention to one pupil by testing whether each student could kill a bird where no one could see; the pupil returned his bird alive because God sees everywhere.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض الصالحين له تلامذة وكان يخص واحدا منهم بإقباله عليه أكثر مما يقبل على غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses ما rather than من because the intended sense is descriptive.
rows.anchor: ذكر ما دون من لأنه أريد به الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من النساء explains ما نكح, and fathers figuratively includes grandfathers.
rows.anchor: وقوله من النساء بيان لما نكح واسم الآباء ينتظم الأجداد مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs married their fathers' wives, so the verse forbids marrying women whom one's fathers married.
rows.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يتزوجون بأزواج آبائهم فنهوا عن ذلك أي لا تنكحوا التي نكحها آباؤكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception about what is past is attached to the forbidden marriages and rhetorically makes the ban emphatic by presenting only an impossible exception; it closes every route to permission.
rows.anchor: استثناء مما نكح مفيد للمبالغة في التحريم بإخراج الكلام مخرج التعليق بالمحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with a camel entering a needle's eye illustrates the impossible conditional form used to block permission entirely.
rows.anchor: المقصود سد طريق الإباحة بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The marriage is called fahisha because it is an ugly act and grave sin before God, never licensed to any community; maqt means intense hatred among honorable people.
rows.anchor: أي فعلة قبيحة ومعصية شديدة عند الله ما رخص فيه لأمة من الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وساء سبيلا is parsed as an accusative of specification: it condemns this as an evil path that leads its practitioner to Hell.
rows.anchor: نصب على التمييز أي بئس السبيل سبيل من يراه ويفعله فإنه يؤدي صاحبه إلى النار

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported analysis assigns rational ugliness to fahisha, religious ugliness to maqt, and customary ugliness to evil way; their combination makes the act maximally vile.
rows.anchor: قيل : مراتب القبح ثلاث : القبح العقلي وإليه أشير بقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, fathers signify the celestial realms and mothers the lower realms; their union produces created beings between them.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن الآباء هي العلويات والأمهات هي السفليات وبازدواجهما خلق الله تعالى المتولدات منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition inwardly warns against attaching oneself to and acting within the lower realm over which the celestial fathers preside.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى نهي التعلق والتصرف في السفليات التي هي الأمهات المتصرفة فيها آباؤكم العلوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for the past alludes to God's prior ordering of the union of spirits and bodies, to which human necessities are bound.
rows.anchor: من التدبير الإلهي في ازدواج الأرواح والأشباح فالحاجات الضرورية للإنسان مسيسة به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attachment, reliance, and immersion in lower things stain the spiritual substance with animal traits, make it low and distant from the divine presence, and turn it toward worldly love and forgetfulness of God.
rows.anchor: يعني التصرف في السفليات والتعلق بها والركون إليها مما يلوث الجوهر الروحاني بلوث الصفات الحيوانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such worldly attachment incurs the Real's displeasure and turns the path to guidance into misguidance.
rows.anchor: ويجعله سفلي الطبع بعيدا عن الحضرة محبا للدنيا ناسيا للرب ممقوتا للحق وساء سبيلا إلى الهداية بالضلالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of mothers means prohibition of marrying them, as customary usage understands a forbidden thing through its intended use: marrying women, drinking wine, and eating pork.
rows.anchor: لأن المفهوم في العرف من حرمة كل شيء ما هو الغرض المقصود منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mothers includes all ascending grandmothers through either parent; daughters includes biological daughters and all descendants; sisters includes full, paternal, and maternal sisters.
rows.anchor: والأمهات تعم الجدات وإن غلون من الأب والأم أو من قبل إحداهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bans on mothers and daughters have held from Adam to the present in every revealed religion; Zoroaster permitted them, but most Muslims judged him a liar.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن حرمة الأمهات والبنات كانت ثابتة من زمن آدم عليه السلام إلى هذا الزمان ولم يثبت حل نكاحهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says marriage between siblings was permitted in Adam's time only because of necessity.
rows.anchor: أما نكاح الأخوات فقد نقل أن ذلك كان مباحا في زمن آدم عليه السلام وإنما حكم الله بإباحة ذلك على سبيل الضرورة

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam explains that intercourse is humiliating and usually hidden, so mothers must be protected from it because their benefaction is greatest; daughters are part of oneself and likewise must be spared this humiliation, as must the other listed relatives.
rows.anchor: وذكر العلماء أن السبب لهذا التحريم أن الوطء إذلال وإهانة فإن الإنسان يستحيي من ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A paternal aunt is any female child of one's father, near or distant; a maternal aunt is any female child of one's mother, likewise including sisters of ancestors through either side.
rows.anchor: العمة كل أنثى ولدها من ولد والدك قريبا أو بعيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nieces of brothers and sisters from every side, including their descendants however remote, are forbidden.
rows.anchor: من كل جهة ونوافلهما وإن بعدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names fourteen forbidden categories: seven by lineage and seven by cause, then begins the latter list with nursing mothers and milk sisters.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى نص على تحريم أربعة عشر صنفا من النسوان سبع منهن من جهة النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nursing mothers and milk sisters are forbidden like their counterparts by lineage; God gives the wet nurse the status of mother and a nursing partner the status of sister.
rows.anchor: أي حرم نكاح الأمهات والأخوات كلتاهما من الرضاعة كما حرمتا من النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wet nurse’s husband is the nursling’s father and his parents are grandparents; his children by other women are paternal siblings, while the wet nurse’s mother and sister are grandmother and aunt.
rows.anchor: وكذلك زوج المرضعة أبوه وأبواه جداه وأخته عمته وكل ولد ولد له من غير المرضعة قبل الإرضاع وبعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wet nurse’s children by that husband are full siblings; her children by another husband are maternal siblings.
rows.anchor: وكل من ولد لها من هذا الزوج فهم إخوته وأخواته لأبيه وأمه ومن ولد لها من غيره فهم إخوته وأخواته لأمه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet states the general rule that nursing forbids the same relations forbidden by lineage.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم "يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Certain apparent milk relations are forbidden through affinity rather than lineage, including a father’s partner, a man’s partner’s daughter or mother, and a grandfather’s partner.
rows.anchor: وأما أم أخيه لأب وأخت ابنه لأم وأم أم ابنه وأم عمه وأم خاله لأب ليست حرمتهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mothers of wives means women married to the men, whether or not the marriage was consummated.
rows.anchor: المراد بالنساء المنكوحات على الإطلاق سواء كن مدخولا بهن أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority hold that a wife's mother is forbidden whether or not the marriage was consummated; a Prophetic report allows marrying the daughter after divorce before consummation but forbids marrying the mother.
rows.anchor: جمهور العلماء وقد روي عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال في رجل تزوج امرأة

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly ruled that a man divorced before consummation may marry his former wife's daughter but may not marry her mother.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال في رجل تزوج امرأة ثم طلقها قبل الدخول بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rules also extend to women touched or otherwise sexually contacted, and mothers includes wet nurses and grandmothers.
rows.anchor: ويلحق بهن الموطوءات بوجه من الوجوه المعدودات فيما سبق آنفا والممسوسات ونظائرهن وأمهات تعم المرضعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rabiiba is a wife's daughter from another man, so named because a stepfather commonly raises her as he raises his own child; the term is an intensive form with passive sense, made into a noun by the feminine ending.
rows.anchor: الربيب ولد المرأة من آخر سمي به لأنه يربه كما يرب ولده في غالب الأمر فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says حجر has two pronunciations and denotes the cloth gathered over a person's thighs; in the verse, being in one's حجر means being raised in one's care.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت حجر الإنسان وحجره بالفتح والكسر هو ما يجمع على فخذيه من ثوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lap is a metaphor for upbringing because a caregiver seats a child there; it is comparable to being in someone's custody, from حضن, the armpit.
rows.anchor: والسبب في هذه الاستعارة أن كل من ربى طفلا أجلسه في حجره فصار الحجر عبارة عن التربية

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority do not require a stepdaughter to have lived in her stepfather's care for the marriage prohibition to apply; the phrase reflects the usual situation, as wives with grown daughters rarely remarry while those with young children often do.
rows.anchor: كون التربية في حجر الراب ليس بشرط للحرمة عند جمهور العلماء والوصف في الآية خرج على الأغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same wording that reflects the usual case is compared with the prohibition of sexual relations during retreat in mosques, although relations outside mosques during retreat are also forbidden.
rows.anchor: والمباشرة في غير المساجد حالة الاعتكاف حرام أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Entering unto the wives means intercourse, expressed euphemistically as admission behind a curtain; touching and similar acts also count, and without intercourse a man may marry the daughters after separation or the mother's death.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الدخول بهن إدخالهن الستر والباء للتعدية وهي كناية عن الجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase حَلائل أبناءكم names sons' wives; حليلة is explained either by a wife's being lawful to her husband, living in his place, or each partner's access to the other's garment.
rows.anchor: أي : وحرم عليكم زوجات أبنائكم سميت الزوجة حليلة لحلها للزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition also covers women illicitly approached by one's son and comparable cases of touching or sexual contact.
rows.anchor: وفي حكمهن مزنياتهم ومن يجري مجراهن من الممسوسات ونظائرهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase sons from your loins excludes adopted sons, while sons' descendants and milk sons, however far down, count as sons by lineage for this rule.
rows.anchor: لإخراج الأدعياء دون أبناء الأولاد والأبناء من الرضاع فإنهم وإن سفلوا في حكم الأبناء الصلبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adoptive father may marry the former wife of an adopted son; Muhammad married Zaynab after Zayd, whom he had adopted, divorced her, and critics were answered by revelation.
rows.anchor: وقد تزوج النبي عليه السلام زينب ابنة جحش الأسدية بنت عمته أميمة ابنة عبد المطلب حين فارقها زيد بن حارثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Combining two sisters in marriage is forbidden, while their simultaneous ownership is not; combining intercourse with both under ownership is included by implication because the operative basis is shared.
rows.anchor: أي وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين في النكاح لا في ملك اليمين وأما جمعهما في الوطء بملك اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception for past conduct is disconnected: past acts are not held against people; God forgives pre-Islamic conduct and is merciful to those who repent and obey.
rows.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن ما قد مضى لا تؤاخذون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite in the lowest levels is like a fruitless tree uprooted from the garden and used as fuel.
rows.anchor: والمنافق في الدركات كشجرة غير مثمرة تقلع من البستان وتوقد بها النار

rows.speaker: فردوسي
rows.claim: Ferdowsi's couplet contrasts the rooted, fruitful tree left in the garden with the barren tree uprooted and burned.
rows.anchor: من البستان وتوقد بها النار ، قال الفردوسي :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here كتبنا means We imposed or prescribed the duty on these hypocrites.
rows.anchor: أي : أوجبنا أو فرضنا على هؤلاء المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing oneself or leaving one's home recalls the duty imposed on the Israelites when they sought repentance for their sins.
rows.anchor: كما أوجبناه على بني إسرائيل حين طلبوا التوبة من ذنوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only a few, the sincere, would have carried out the prescribed duty.
rows.anchor: إلا ناس قليل منهم وهم المخلصون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Doing what they are admonished means following and obeying the Messenger, marching under his banner, and submitting outwardly and inwardly to his judgment.
rows.anchor: من متابعة الرسول وطاعته والمشي تحت رايته والانقياد لما يراه ويحكم به ظاهرا وباطنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's commands and prohibitions are called admonitions because they pair promise and threat with encouragement and warning.
rows.anchor: وسميت أوامر الله ونواهيه مواعظ لاقترانها بالوعد والوعيد والترغيب والترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience would be better for them, bringing the best outcome in both worlds.
rows.anchor: أي : أحمد عاقبة في الدارين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the admonition would make them more firmly established in faith and less prone to instability.
rows.anchor: لهم على الإيمان وأبعد من الاضطراب فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stood firm, God would grant them abundant, everlasting reward in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ثوابا كثيرا في الآخرة لا ينقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would guide them on a straight path to the holy realm and open the doors of the unseen to them.
rows.anchor: يصلون بسلوكه إلى عالم القدس ويفتح لهم أبواب الغيب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever acts on what he knows will inherit from God knowledge he did not know.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "من عمل بما علم ورثه الله علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, killing the self means subduing the ego's desire, which is its life, and annihilating its traits.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن قتل النفس في الحقيقة قمع هواها التي هي حياتها وإفناء صفاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly leaving one's homes means leaving familiar stations lodged in the heart—patience, trust, contentment, and surrender—because they veil unity and self-annihilation in the divine essence.
rows.anchor: والخروج من الديار خروج من المقامات التي سكنت القلوب بها وألفتها من الصبر والتوكل والرضى والتسليم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Ibrahim described roaming deserts and wilderness without water, trees, gardens, or rain when asked about his state and whether this was trust in God.
rows.anchor: لإبراهيم بن أدهم حين سأله عن حاله وأجابه بقوله أدور في الصحاري وأطوف في البراري

rows.speaker: الحسين بن منصور
rows.claim: Al-Husayn ibn Mansur challenged Ibrahim that spending one's life cultivating the inner self raises the question of where annihilation in divine unity has gone.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحسين بن منصور لإبراهيم بن أدهم حين سأله عن حاله وأجابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obedience to God and the Messenger means complete submission and full compliance with every command and prohibition.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالطاعة هو الانقياد التام والامتثال الكامل بجميع الأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: ثوبان
rows.claim: Thawban came to the Prophet visibly changed and thin, explaining that he was healthy but missed him intensely and feared that their different ranks in the next life would keep them apart.
rows.anchor: روي أن ثوبان مولى رسول الله أتاه يوما وقد تغير وجهه ونحل جسمه فسأله عن حاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says the verse was revealed about Thawban's fear of being unable to see the Prophet in the afterlife because he would be at a lower rank.
rows.anchor: ما بي من وجع غير أني إذا لم أرك اشتقت إليك واستوحشت وحشة شديدة على لقائك ثم ذكرت الآخرة فخفت أن لا أراك هناك لأني

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet swore that a servant does not truly believe until he loves him more than himself, parents, family, children, and all people.
rows.anchor: فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم "والذي نفسي بيده لا يؤمن عبد حتى أكون أحب إليه من نفسه وأبويه وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those points to the obedient, and being with those God blessed means receiving His complete blessing; the promise encourages obedience with the company of God's nearest and highest-ranking servants.
rows.anchor: فأولئك إشارة إلى المطيعين {مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets possess complete knowledge and action and pass beyond personal perfection to perfecting others.
rows.anchor: بيان للمنعم عليهم وهم الفائزون بكمال العلم والعمل المتجاوزون حد الكمال إلى درجة التكميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truthful are exceptionally sincere in word and deed; through reasoning from proofs and spiritual discipline they reach gnosis and perceive things as they are.
rows.anchor: المبالغين في الصدق والإخلاص في الأقوال والأفعال الذين صعدت نفوسهم تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The martyrs are those whose zeal for obedience and publicizing truth led them to give their lives to exalt God's word.
rows.anchor: الذين أدى بهم الحرص على الطاعة والجد في إظهار الحق حتى بذلوا مهجهم في إعلاء كلمة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous devote their lives to obedience and their wealth to God's good pleasure.
rows.anchor: الذين صرفوا أعمارهم في طاعته وأموالهم في مرضاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being with these people does not mean equal rank or merely entering Paradise together; it means being able to see and visit one another whenever desired, however far apart.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد بالمعية الاتحاد في الدرجة لأن التساوي بين الفاضل والمفضول لا يجوز ولا مطلق الاشتراك في دخول الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How good companions is an exclamation of admiration; رفيقا is an accusative of specification, singular in form though used for one or many, and derives from gentleness in association.
rows.anchor: في معنى التعجب كأنه قيل وما أحسن أولئك رفيقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That bounty denotes the obedient people's great reward, added guidance, and companionship with the blessed; it comes from God alone, who knows the reward and who deserves His grace.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ والفضل صفته وهو إشارة إلى ما للمطيعين من عظيم الأجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest refusal to worship God is associating partners with Him and turning from divine unity; unity and faith are the foundation of all deeds.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن أعظم الاستنكاف عن عبادة الله تعالى الشرك والإعراض عن توحيده كما أن أصل الأعمال التوحيد والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pride is among the greatest sins, and a reported Prophetic saying contrasts a mustard seed of pride, which bars Paradise, with an atom of faith, which bars Hell.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال حبة من خردل من كبر

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi's couplet warns that when lust, pride, greed, envy, and treachery within the self gain strength, they rebel against one's judgment and command.
rows.anchor: من إيمان" ، قال السعدي قدس سره :

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: Abu Yazid told a judge who knew religious teachings but felt no effect to carry walnuts at his neck and offer one to anyone who slapped him, as a cure for pride.
rows.anchor: حكي أن قاضيا جاء إلى أبي يزيد البسطامي رحمه الله يوما فقال : نحن نعرف ما تعرفه

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: When the judge apologized, Abu Yazid said he had erred by seeking a remedy for his pride and then asking pardon from the very humiliation meant to cure it.
rows.anchor: فاستغفر القاضي فقال أبو يزيد : قد أذنبت لأني أذكر ما يخلصك

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdi's verses say a self-satisfied person should not expect to hear truth, and that admonition cannot make a stony heart bloom, just as rain cannot make flowers grow from stone.
rows.anchor: وأنت تستغفر منه ، قال السعدي :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sensible person should be humble, since elevation comes through humility and humility is among the best acts of worship.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتواضع فإن الرفعة في التواضع وهو من أفضل العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address يا أيها الناس is directed to all morally responsible people.
rows.anchor: يا اأيها الناس} خطاب لعامة المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof from God means miracles and the manifest light sent through the Prophet means the Qur'an; together they provide rational and transmitted evidence, leaving no excuse.
rows.anchor: عنى بالبرهان المعجزات وبالنور القرآن أي جاءكم دلائل العقل وشواهد النقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Burhan means that by which a claim is demonstrated; the Qur'an is called light because it creates faith's light in hearts and clarifies rulings as light reveals objects.
rows.anchor: والبرهان ما يبرهن به المطلوب وسمي القرآن نورا لكونه سببا لوقوع نور الإيمان في القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believing in God according to the proof and holding fast to Him means sheltering oneself from the commanding ego and Satan's insinuations.
rows.anchor: أي امتنعوا به عن اتباع النفس الأمارة وتسويلات الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy is reward proportionate to faith and deeds, granted as grace rather than as a debt.
rows.anchor: ثواب قدره بإزاء إيمانه وعمله رحمة منه لا قضاء لحق واجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s additional favor exceeds anything seen, heard, or imagined.
rows.anchor: إحسان زائد عليه مما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being guided to God means guidance along Islam and obedience in this life and the path to Paradise in the next, all leading to Him.
rows.anchor: هو الإسلام والطاعة في الدنيا وطريق الجنة في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, صراطا مستقيما is a second direct object of هدى, which can take two objects directly or take the second with إلى; إليه is an anticipatory circumstantial phrase, or would qualify صراط if delayed.
rows.anchor: وهو مفعول ثان ليهدي لأنه يتعدى إلى مفعولين بنفسه كما يتعدى إلى الثاني بإلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ماذا combines the interrogative ما with relative ذا and asks what foods have been made lawful.
rows.anchor: ما للاستفهام وذا بمعنى الذي والمعنى ما الذي أحل لهم من المطاعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayyib means tasty and desired; what counts as pleasant is judged by people of honorable, fine character, while desert Arabs consider all animals good to eat.
rows.anchor: والطيب في اللغة المستلذ المشتهى فالتقدير كل ما يستلذ ويشتهي والعبرة في الاستلذاذ والاستطابة بأهل المروءة

rows.speaker: الإمام في تفسيره
rows.claim: The Imam's commentary says desert people find all animals pleasant to eat, supplying the criterion for what is tayyib.
rows.anchor: فإن أهل البادية يستطيبون أكل جميع الحيوانات كذا قال الإمام في تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وما علمتم is coordinated with الطيبات by supplying an implied noun meaning the game of what you have trained; ما is relative with its pronoun omitted.
rows.anchor: عطف على الطيبات بتقدير المضاف على أن ما موصولة والعائد محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الجوارح is a circumstantial phrase and plural of جارحة, meaning an acquiring animal; it may also derive from wounding, since hunting animals often tear prey.
rows.anchor: حال من الموصول جمع جارحة بمعنى كاسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term covers any trainable animal that catches game for its owner, including hunting mammals such as cheetahs, leopards, and dogs, and birds such as falcons and eagles; their catches are lawful.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالجوارح في الآية كل ما يكسب الصيد على أهله من سباع البهائم كالفهد والنمر والكلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مكلبين means training and inciting hunting animals; it comes from dog because dogs are especially receptive to hunting instruction, and is an accusative circumstantial phrase attached to the trainer.
rows.anchor: أي معلمين لها الصيد والمكلب مؤدب الجوارح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the trainers مكلبين stresses their expertise: the title applies only to a highly skilled trainer, so the phrase means they are adept and renowned in training.
rows.anchor: فائدتها المبالغة في التعليم لما أن اسم المكلب لا يقع إلا على النحرير في علمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تعلمونهن is a second circumstantial phrase; God taught people the techniques of training, whether by inspiration, reason as a divine gift, or learned methods such as sending, calling back, stopping, and having the animal hold prey without eating it.
rows.anchor: حال ثانية {مما علمكم الله} من الحيل وطرق التعليم والتأديب

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the verse teaches that students should learn from a deeply expert master who knows a field's subtleties, even if reaching that teacher requires a long journey.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب "الكشاف" قوله تعالى : {تعلمونهن مما علمكم الله} فيه تنبيه على أن كل من يأخذ علما ينبغي أن يأخذه

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying urges seekers to pursue knowledge even as far away as China.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "اطلبوا العلم ولو بالصين"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Learning from someone unqualified wastes one's days and leaves one regretting it when meeting the true experts.
rows.anchor: فكم من آخذ من غير متقن ضيع أيامه وعض عند لقاء النحارير أنامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partitive من means eat some of what the animal held, omitting inedible hides, bones, and feathers; the relative pronoun has an omitted antecedent, and على marks what was held for the hunter.
rows.anchor: من تبعيضية لما أن البعض مما لا يتعلق به الأكل كالجلود والعظام والريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eat only the prey the trained animal has not eaten; if it ate from the prey, it held it for itself, as the Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim, and most jurists agree.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي لم يأكلن منه وأما ما أكلن منه فهو مما أمسكن على أنفسهن لقوله عليه السلام لعدي بن حاتم

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet told ʿAdi ibn Hatim not to eat prey from which the hunting animal has eaten, since it caught that prey for itself.
rows.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام لعدي بن حاتم : "وإن أكل منه فلا تأكل إنما أمسكه على نفسه"

rows.speaker: بعضهم ومنهم أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Some jurists, including Abu Hanifa, allow the remainder of prey caught by a trained bird but not by a dog, since a dog can be trained not to eat by beating whereas a hawk cannot.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم ومنهم أبو حنيفة : يؤكل مما بقي من جوارح الطير ولا يؤكل مما بقي من الكلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in واذكروا اسم الله عليه may refer to what was trained, requiring invocation when releasing it, or to the prey held, requiring invocation when slaughtering it.
rows.anchor: الضمير لما في علمتم أي سموا عليه عند إرساله أو لما في ما أمسكن أي سموا عليه إذا أدركتم ذكاته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In Abu Thaʿlaba's report, the Prophet says to avoid the People of the Book's utensils if alternatives exist, or wash them if not; eat game taken with a bow or trained dog when God's name was invoked, and eat an untrained dog's catch only if it is found alive and slaughtered.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي ثعلبة قال : قلت يا نبي الله إنا بأرض قوم أهل كتاب أفنأكل في آنيتهم

rows.speaker: أنس رضي الله عنه
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet sacrificed two white, horned rams by his own hand, saying God's name and magnifying Him.
rows.anchor: وعن أنس رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم "كان يضحي بكبشين أملحين أقرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recommended formula is بسم الله الله أكبر without و because the conjunction would cut off the light of the basmala, according to Sharh Mukhtasar al-Wiqaya.
rows.anchor: والمستحب أن يقول بسم الله الله أكبر بلا واو لأن ذكر الواو يقطع نور التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the qibla orientation is disliked, while the sacrifice remains valid, as stated in al-Dhakhira.
rows.anchor: وكره ترك التوجه إلى القبلة وحلت كذا في "الذخيرة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deliberately omitting God's name makes the animal carrion and forbidden, while forgetting to invoke it leaves the meat lawful.
rows.anchor: ومتروك التسمية عمدا حرام لأنه ميتة بخلاف متروكها نسيانا فإنه حلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa here means observing God's prohibitions; سريع الحساب means either that reckoning arrives soon or that it is completed quickly once begun, so God accounts for every small and great matter swiftly.
rows.anchor: في شأن محرماته {إن الله سريع الحساب} سريع إتيان حسابه أو سريع تمامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that hunting is lawful.
rows.anchor: ودلت الآية على إباحة الصيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, spiritual seekers ask what is lawful or forbidden to them in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن أرباب الطلب وأصحاب السلوك

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A reported saying says the world is forbidden to the people of the hereafter, the hereafter to the people of the world, and both to God's own people.
rows.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "الدنيا حرام على أهل الآخرة والآخرة حرام على أهل الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, the good things are whatever do not interrupt one's way of reaching God.
rows.anchor: وهي ما لا يقطع عليكم طريق الوصول إلى الله فإن الله طيب لا يقبل إلا الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is pure and accepts only the pure, whatever one consumes, wears, says, thinks, or does from self-interest is tainted by the ego's self-directed impulse and is spiritually foul.
rows.anchor: وكل مأكول ومشروب وملبوس ومقول ومعقول ومعمول طلبتموه بحظ من الحظوظ فقد لوثتموه للوث داعي الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What one seeks sincerely to fulfill obligations, purified by the breath of spiritual witnessing, is among the good things and suits the good.
rows.anchor: وما طلبتموه بالحق للقيام بأداء الحقوق مطيبا بنفحات الشهود فهو من الطيبات لا يصلح إلا للطيبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, God reckons people before they finish their deeds and repays them immediately: good brings intimacy, rank, and providential attraction; evil brings distance, expulsion, abasement, and abandonment.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى يحاسب العباد على أعمالهم قبل أن يفرغوا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous maxim says each person acts for himself: whoever does wrong harms himself, and whoever does good does good for himself.
rows.anchor: نعم ما قيل : (هركه كند بخود كند ورهمه نيك بد كند)

rows.speaker: الصائب
rows.claim: Al-Saʾib's couplet portrays one's own desire as the constant destroyer of one's inner home.
rows.anchor: هركه كند بخود كند ورهمه نيك بد كند) قال الصائب :
